title: Compact objects are closed under small simplicial colimits
statement: Use quasicategories, spaces, coherent diagrams and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the universes, $\kappa$-smallness, $\kappa$-filteredness and $\kappa$-compactness from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Let $\kappa$ be an infinite regular cardinal in the smaller universe. Let $\mathcal C$ be a locally small quasicategory admitting all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Let $K$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial set and $p:K\to\mathcal C$ a coherent diagram such that $p(v)$ is $\kappa$-compact for every vertex $v\in K_0$. If $p$ admits a colimiting cocone with apex $c$, then $c$ is $\kappa$-compact. In particular the empty diagram is allowed: an initial object, when it exists, is $\kappa$-compact.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.15, printed p. 398 (closure of kappa-compact objects under existing kappa-small colimits). Read online (March 10, 2012 text), not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Let $F:I\to\mathcal C$ be any coherent diagram indexed by a small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory, with a colimiting cocone and apex $d$. For each vertex $v\in K_0$, the $\kappa$-compactness of $p(v)$ gives a natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p(v),d)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p(v),F(i))$. This is exactly the mapping-space clause in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], applied to the vertex object $p(v)$. Write $a_v$ for this canonical map in the direction from the colimit to the mapping space. Functoriality of precomposition makes the $a_v$ a coherent transformation of $K^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagrams.

source.place: Definition 5.3.4.5, printed p. 393; Corollary 5.3.4.15, printed p. 398

proof.text: Because the given cocone $p\to c$ is colimiting, the coherent Yoneda mapping-space criterion [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identifies, naturally in $d$, $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,d)$ with the $K$-shaped limit $\lim_{v\in K^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p(v),d)$. The opposite indexing is the one in the cited statement for a cocone.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.15, printed p. 398, using the coherent mapping-space criterion

proof.text: Put $X(v,i)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p(v),F(i))$, a coherent diagram $K^{\mathrm{op}}\times I\to\mathcal S$. Its values are small up to equivalence by local smallness. Reversing the order of simplices preserves nondegeneracy and their number, so $K^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $\kappa$-small. The canonical maps $a_v$ of Step 1 are equivalences at every vertex, hence form an equivalence of coherent diagrams by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Applying the limit functor gives an equivalence $\lim_v\operatorname{colim}_i X(v,i)\to\lim_v\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p(v),d)$. Since $I$ is small and $\kappa$-filtered, [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] gives the equivalence $q:\operatorname{colim}_i\lim_v X(v,i)\to\lim_v\operatorname{colim}_i X(v,i)$. Thus the composite $(\lim_v a_v)\circ q$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3.3, printed pp. 391-392, and Corollary 5.3.4.15, printed p. 398

proof.text: For each $i$, [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] gives the natural equivalence $r_i:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,F(i))\to\lim_v X(v,i)$; Step 2 gives $r_d$ with target $\lim_v\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(p(v),d)$. Let $b:\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,F(i))\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,d)$ be the compactness comparison. The coherent diagram formed by these maps satisfies $r_d\circ b\simeq(\lim_v a_v)\circ q\circ\operatorname{colim}_i r_i$: restricting along the $i$th colimit cocone and the $v$th limit projection, both composites send a map $h:c\to F(i)$ to $p(v)\to c\xrightarrow{h}F(i)\to d$; the coherences are those of the two given cocones and functorial composition. Thus the equality holds for the entire induced cone, not only its vertices. Both $r_d$ and the right-hand composite are equivalences, so $b$ is an equivalence. Since $F$ was arbitrary, [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] makes $c$ $\kappa$-compact. For $K=\varnothing$, the same proof uses the empty limit, namely the terminal space, and the empty-shape clause of the interchange theorem. For $K=\Delta^0$, it recovers precisely the assumed compactness of $p(v)$.

split_report.summary: Mapping-space compactness calculation, with coherent vertexwise comparison, explicit canonical-map compatibility, and one auxiliary κ-small-limit/κ-filtered-colimit theorem for small diagrams of spaces.
split_report.blueprint: Technical foundational input along the recorded ancestry from lem-coef-space-presheaf-presentability to prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, serving its second proof paragraph: the displayed finite-coefficient mapping-complex adjunction before the derived inverse limit. The current main-20261015 proof has no literal compactness clause; the four steps prove the supporting compactness lemma rather than attribute that sentence to the blueprint.

tool_uses.why: Its vertexwise criterion recognizes the coherent canonical compactness transformation as an equivalence; this is a general quasicategory tool, not a replacement for a unit step.
